correctness.rationale: The affine reflected-gradient recurrence reduces exactly to a quadratic characteristic equation for each eigenvalue of the operator matrix. Strong monotonicity and the spectral-norm bound give a half-disk spectral enclosure. Parameterizing a unit-modulus characteristic root, eliminating the angular variable, and enforcing both enclosure constraints yields the unique cubic threshold. Strict stability below it follows by continuity from small positive steps, and a two-dimensional normal rotation-dilation matrix attains the boundary. Symbolic checks verify the elimination, derivative, endpoints, representative contact, and numerical specialization.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 source paper gives the sharp merely-monotone affine threshold 1/sqrt(3) and a separate conservative strong-monotonicity rate theorem, but does not state the exact condition-ratio-dependent interpolation. Earlier reflected-gradient papers establish linear convergence under strong monotonicity, while the closest sharp OGD control result assumes cocoercivity in addition to strong monotonicity. No located source gives the cubic threshold or matching rotation-dilation extremizer for the affine strong-monotone-plus-Lipschitz class. Originality is asserted only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp universal stepsize law for an important affine subclass, strictly improves the condition-independent 1/sqrt(3) ceiling whenever the strong-monotonicity margin is positive, interpolates to the 2/3 scalar endpoint, identifies the exact extremal operator, and quantitatively explains the stability margin of the source paper's strongly monotone planar example.
